record.original_question: What physical conditions determine the gamma-ray-burst/supernova connection: why do many supernovae, including Type Ic events, not produce observable gamma-ray bursts, and why do many gamma-ray bursts lack associated supernovae?

evidence.quote: It is now well established that a number of Gamma-Ray Burst (GRB) sources have associated SNIc counterparts (e.g. [24]) and that both SNIc and GRBs are most closely associated with active star forming regions than any other type of explosive sources [25].

However, only a handful of GRBs-SNIc associations have been recognized so far and, despite all efforts, there are GRBs that are positively not associated with any SN, e.g. GRB 060614 for which it has been excluded the association with any SN brighter than -13.7 [22, 23], and many SNIc that have not shown evidence of any conspicuous gamma-ray emission (e.g. [24]).
Therefore, we are presented with two complementary and fundamental questions: “Why many SNe are not GRBs?", and “Why many GRBs are not SNe?".
Only answering these questions, we could claim that we do understand the GRB-SN connection.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Long-duration gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) are brief, intense flashes of high-energy gamma radiation observed at cosmological distances, while Type Ic supernovae (SNe Ic) are stellar explosions arising from the core collapse of massive stars whose envelopes have been stripped of hydrogen and helium. Observationally, certain GRBs have been firmly associated with broad-lined Type Ic supernovae, and both phenomena tend to occur in active star-forming regions. Yet only a small fraction of detected GRBs show an accompanying supernova (with some events, such as GRB 060614, ruling out any associated supernova brighter than absolute magnitude -13.7), and the vast majority of Type Ic supernovae show no detectable gamma-ray burst counterpart.

Identify and characterize the physical conditions—such as progenitor structure (mass, rotation, metallicity, binarity), magnetic field configuration, central engine properties (black hole vs. magnetar formation, accretion rate, jet launching efficiency), envelope/circumstellar properties, and viewing-angle/beaming effects—that determine whether a stripped-envelope core-collapse event produces (a) a successful relativistic jet observable as a GRB, (b) a luminous supernova, both, or neither. In particular, provide a quantitative explanation for the two complementary questions:

(i) Why do many core-collapse supernovae, including Type Ic events, fail to produce observable gamma-ray bursts?
(ii) Why do many gamma-ray bursts have no associated detectable supernova?
artifact.status_search_result: The physical conditions governing the GRB–supernova connection remain an active open question. Recent works (e.g., 2022 detection of a long GRB from a compact-object merger with no associated SN, and 2024 analysis of GRB 221009A whose accompanying SN was unexpectedly ordinary) highlight that the mapping between progenitors, central engines, and observed GRB/SN signatures is still not understood. Reviews and recent observational papers continue to frame the two complementary questions as unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A nearby long gamma-ray burst from a merger of compact objects
status_evidence.snippet: Long GRB with no accompanying supernova, indicating a compact-object merger origin and challenging the collapsar-only picture.
status_evidence.claim: Some long GRBs lack supernova counterparts, indicating diverse progenitors; the GRB-SN mapping is still being elucidated.

status_evidence.title: Brightest gamma-ray burst of all time came from the collapse of a massive star
status_evidence.snippet: The supernova accompanying GRB 221009A was unexpectedly normal, raising open questions about why extreme GRB energetics do not correlate with SN brightness.
status_evidence.claim: The relation between GRB energetics and SN luminosity is not understood, supporting open status.

status_evidence.title: The Observer's Guide to the Gamma-Ray Burst Supernova Connection
status_evidence.snippet: Review noting that only a fraction of long GRBs show SN signatures and only broad-lined SNe Ic are linked to GRBs, with the underlying conditions still debated.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference review treats the GRB-SN connection physical conditions as open.
